video.title: A stack of neurons: one cut, then a bend
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. A small network trains on a ring; code and equations stay left to right in both languages. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Joseph - computer studies teacher, talking to a fellow lecturer
Narrator - the Darsi voice, warm and precise, talking to a university lecturer

scenes.visual: A ring of points, and a straight line that misses it.
scenes.animation: The line appears, then the missed points.
scenes.narration: Many students think a deeper network is simply a smarter one. Show them a ring of points no straight line can separate, and ask which part bends the line.
In the seminar: what one neuron can cut, and why the activation, not the extra layer alone, does the bending.

scenes.animation: Each card arrives with its sentence.
scenes.narration: A neuron is a weighted sum, a bias, and an activation. The weights say how much each input counts, and the bias shifts the sum before the bend.

scenes.visual: One neuron beside a stack with no activation. Both are one cut.
scenes.animation: The two columns appear in turn.
scenes.narration: One neuron draws one straight cut. Stack linear layers with no activation and they collapse into that same single cut.

scenes.visual: The activation named as the bend.
scenes.animation: The bend arrives on the second sentence.
scenes.narration: The activation is the bend. It lets the next layer turn the previous cut into a curve.

scenes.visual: A small network training on a ring: the boundary wraps, and the loss falls.
scenes.animation: Training plays across the two sentences.
scenes.narration: Here is a ring. A line misses it, and a small network with a hidden layer learns a boundary around it.
Quick check! A single neuron draws which boundary?
One straight cut. A closed curve needs the bend, and more than one layer.

scenes.animation: The steps arrive with the sentences.
scenes.narration: Have pairs name a shape a line misses before anyone opens the playground. Then they run it and say what the hidden layer added.
Your turn. Without an activation, what does a stack of layers become?
Remember this. One neuron makes one cut, and depth bends the boundary only when an activation sits between the layers.

scenes.visual: The hand step: two inputs, two weights, a bias, a ReLU.
scenes.narration: Try it in your next lecture. One phone between two, and the sentence you will mark is what the activation does.

checkpoints.prompt: A single neuron draws which boundary?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct: one neuron is a weighted sum and an activation, and it cuts the plane once.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: one neuron draws one straight cut. A curve needs a bend and more than one layer.

checkpoints.prompt: Without an activation, a stack of layers becomes…
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct: without an activation, stacked linear layers collapse into one cut.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite: without the bend, the stack is still one straight cut.
